insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic attribution that infers purchase intent. A cryptographically verified receipt eliminates the attribution problem entirely — the purchase event is the proof, not a model.

Verified receipt settlement runs ~$0.10 per confirmed conversion against an industry CPA floor of $5. That is a 50–200x cost gap, structural rather than marginal — the kind that rewrites category economics when it scales.

insights.topic: Cookie deprecation leaves no credible replacement in legacy stack
insights.insight: Cookies are dead, device fingerprinting is increasingly blocked, and first-party data is blind outside a single ecosystem. No component of the current ad tech stack produces identity-free, cross-ecosystem, verified purchase signals — which is precisely what this protocol generates.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither knows the other. Any system that surfaces aggregate, anonymized cross-ecosystem purchase behavior creates an intelligence advantage that every brand and retailer is currently missing.

Roughly one-third of 14-day GMV — $35,742 on 131 receipts, averaging $272.84 per ticket — sits in an unresolved merchant category, 6x the basket size of grocery or restaurant. High-ticket and probable B2B transactions are present in volume but not yet classifiable, meaning category-level targeting signals are incomplete.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion pattern signals organic, social-graph propagation
insights.insight: Active metros expanded to non-contiguous zones — rural CA, AR, MI, WI, MA, and Hawaii entered simultaneously with no geographic adjacency — indicating word-of-mouth spread along social graph edges rather than paid acquisition. For brands, this suggests early adopter density in rural and non-metro segments that paid media models would not predict or target.
